It is worth noting that the modularity function used here diﬀers from most standard approaches for dealing with signed networks. Traditionally, signed networks are sub-divided into two separate networks: one containing just positive connections:

Modularity functions are then deﬁned for both the positive and negative components as: Q ± =   ij [ W ± ij − P ± ij ] δ ( g i ,g j ). The choice of how to combine the two components to obtain the total modularity is left up to the user, though a number of weighting schemes have been proposed (G´mez et al., 2009; Rubinov and Sporns, 2011). In general, the total modularity is of the form: Q = c + Q + − c − Q − , where c ± are constants.
